newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Police fire on supporters of slain Bhutto.
newsitem.headline: Police fire on supporters of slain Bhutto.

text.p: Pakistani police fired bullets and teargas to disperse supporters of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's dead brother Murtaza in Larkana on Monday, wounding two of them, witnesses said.

They said 300 to 400 protesters had gathered in the Lahori Mohallah district of Larkana, close to Murtaza's home, the focus of mourning since he was killed in a shootout between his bodyguards and police in Karachi on Friday.
The demonstrators were trying to force shopkeepers to pull down their shutters in line with a 10-day strike called by Murtaza's Pakistan People's Party-Shaheed Bhutto faction.
One protester was wounded in the clash with police.
In a separate incident, police fired at demonstrators approaching Murtaza's house, wounding one.
Murtaza supporters said on Sunday they wanted his Lebanese widow Ghinwa to take over leadership of his breakaway Shaheed Bhutto faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP).
It was not immediately known whether the central coordination committee of the faction had consulted Ghinwa beforehand or whether she would be ready to accept.

Ghinwa had earlier vowed to stay in Pakistan despite Murtaza's death but said she had not decided whether to enter politics, which has brought the charismatic Bhutto family great power and repeated tragedy during the past three decades.

Benazir Bhutto took over the PPP leadership mantle from her father, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who was ousted as prime minister in an army coup in 1977 and executed in 1979 after a controversial conviction for conspiring to murder a political opponent.

Murtaza challenged her leadership when he returned in 1993 after 16 years in self-imposed exile, mainly in Syria. He set up his rival group in March last year, but attracted no political heavyweights from his sister's mainstream party.
But political sources said protests in Murtaza's home province of Sindh and some other parts of Pakistan after his death showed that Murtaza had built up considerable support.

If she accepts the leadership offer, Ghinwa, a former teacher who speaks English and French as well as her native Arabic, would become the first Arab woman to lead a Pakistani political group, although not the first foreign-born.
Her Iranian-born mother-in-law Nusrat became figurehead PPP chief after Zulfikar Bhutto's execution. Benazir engineered her removal as leader in 1993. Nusrat's Iranian roots were not an issue.
Murtaza's supporters also demanded that a Supreme Court judge investigate his killing rather than the provincial high court judge already named by the Sindh province government.
Accusing Benazir's husband of conspiring in Murtaza's death, they fought police in Larkana on Sunday and prevented President Farooq Leghari from paying a condolence call on the family.
They set fire to a police van and motorcyle and stoned private vehicles in Lahore, capital of Punjab province.
